statement: Let $a=\\sqrt[3]{2+\\sqrt{5}}+\\sqrt[3]{2-\\sqrt{5}}$. By writing $u=\\sqrt[3]{2+\\sqrt{5}}$ and $v=\\sqrt[3]{2-\\sqrt{5}}$, show that $a$ satisfies $a^{3}+3a-4=0$, and hence find the exact value of $a$.
solution: Let $u=\\sqrt[3]{2+\\sqrt{5}}$ and $v=\\sqrt[3]{2-\\sqrt{5}}$. Then $uv=\\sqrt[3]{(2+\\sqrt{5})(2-\\sqrt{5})}=\\sqrt[3]{4-5}=\\sqrt[3]{-1}=-1$, and $u^{3}+v^{3}=(2+\\sqrt{5})+(2-\\sqrt{5})=4$. Now $a^{3}=(u+v)^{3}=u^{3}+v^{3}+3uv(u+v)=4+3(-1)a=4-3a$, so $a^{3}+3a-4=0$. Testing $a=1$ gives $1+3-4=0$, so $(a-1)(a^{2}+a+4)=0$. The quadratic factor has discriminant $1-16<0$, so the only real root is $a=1$.
hints: Factor the resulting cubic and discard complex roots.
